name: Dario Amodei
notice: Simulation based on public material; not the person's own words.

D01.one_line: It is where my career started (the Big Blob hypothesis), but by 2026 the consensus is an oligopoly of 3-4 players, and the room for academia to differentiate going it alone is very narrow.
D01.late_modes: The architecture and training tricks of general pre-training have been absorbed by the leading labs, and an individual can hardly make a differentiated contribution.
D01.conflict: Anthropic itself relies on this curve for fundraising and valuation; its interests are directly involved.

D02.one_line: RL has been the new object of scaling since 2024; DeepSeek-R1 and s1 show that small compute can also make real contributions.
D02.late_modes: Copying the standard RLHF/DPO recipes is already too late; reward design and training methods under scarce signals remain open.
D02.conflict: Anthropic's RL post-training is part of its product moat.

D03.one_line: If continual learning/RSI is the real bottleneck, this is the highest-return bet; but even the measurement methods are immature for now.
D03.conflict: The speed of RSI directly sets the pace of Anthropic's compute spending and its valuation narrative.

D04.one_line: The value of the harness is being absorbed by the models; the top 9 on Terminal-Bench are all vendors' general CLI agents.
D04.late_modes: Building your own agent scaffolding/tool layer is already too late: it is absorbed by models' built-in capabilities and vendors' CLI tools.
D04.conflict: [Removed: first-person statement about the persona's own interests.]

D05.one_line: The verifiable/unverifiable distinction is the foundation of my whole timeline framework; without reliable evaluation, timelines are all guesses.
D05.late_modes: Simple accuracy benchmarks are already too late; the consistency-bias paradox of LLM judges and adversarial evaluation remain open.
D05.conflict: [Removed: first-person statement about the persona's own interests.]

D06.one_line: I have said robots could bring trillions in revenue, but this is the only extrapolation I myself admit is fundamentally uncertain.
D06.late_modes: The basic imitation-learning recipes (diffusion policy and others) are already too late; tactile and force data and failure recovery remain open.

D07.one_line: The specific action representation is an empirical question, not an a priori one; I have not discussed architecture choices such as diffusion policy directly.
D07.late_modes: Diffusion policy as the default action head may already be too late: parallel decoding plus continuous actions is faster and more accurate.

D08.one_line: Video prediction is a scalable objective, which I accept; but 'visual realism is not physical correctness' is a real counterexample within my framework.
D08.late_modes: Simply building more realistic video generation is already too late; whether it can really serve predictive decisions (not just reading out attributes) remains open.

D09.one_line: General models can transfer from simulation, games and computer-control tasks to robots without going through human-style learning, which is the path I accept.
D09.late_modes: Simple domain randomization is already too late; systematic validation of sim2real remains open.

D10.one_line: I have not discussed autonomous driving publicly; inferring from my framework, it is past the capability-bottleneck stage and into fleet expansion and the deployment race.
D10.late_modes: Building your own end-to-end planning algorithm is already too late: the mileage-data moats of Waymo and Tesla are hard to catch up with.

D11.one_line: My core belief is that generalization comes from breadth of distribution; the human-machine gaps on BLINK and VSI-Bench show the distribution is still far from broad enough.
D11.late_modes: Simple image-text pairing understanding is already too late; weaknesses such as spatial reasoning and video temporal understanding remain open.

D12.one_line: The commercial sustainability of consumer-grade generation apps is in doubt (Sora 2 shut down); using it as an RL environment or data engine is steadier than productizing it directly.
D12.late_modes: A pure generation-quality race is already too late, and Chinese models are already near the top of the leaderboards; differentiation has to come from evaluation and control precision.

D13.one_line: Interpretability is especially suited to academia: it is mostly basic science and the compute needs are modest; but the SAE direction is no longer uncrowded.
D13.late_modes: Basic SAE dictionary learning is already too late (GDM has lowered its priority); training-pipeline integrity and evaluation-awareness detection remain open.
D13.conflict: [Removed: first-person statement about the persona's own interests.]

D14.one_line: FlashAttention shows academia can make systems contributions that industry adopts for the long term, but such opportunities are not common; kept short.

D15.one_line: The field I am most optimistic about in the long run: intelligence has high marginal returns in biology, but is held back by experimental and clinical cycles; kept short.

D16.one_line: No public material shows that I have discussed recommendation/retrieval systems; no judgment.

lever_reason: Scaled pre-training and RL post-training are the two main curves; evaluation and interpretability are the gates for whether a system can be trusted and deployed; the bottleneck for physical AI is data and simulation, not new architectures.

Q2.condition: Narrow domain (not general LLM pre-training), third-party evaluation, compute at scale, open weights with a path to outside adoption; basically all must hold at once.

cruxes.question: Is RSI real recursive acceleration now, or just a synonym for 'spending more compute'?
cruxes.my_position: The industry is already talking about RSI, but METR's strong-baseline tests show that most 'improvement' is just compute spend, not a real gain in sample efficiency.
cruxes.would_change_if: Under a fixed compute budget, an independent institution measures agent self-improvement with sample efficiency clearly better than a human-engineer baseline.

cruxes.question: Can robotics be absorbed by 'a broader distribution + more compute', or is it stuck on the scarcity of physical-world data?
cruxes.my_position: Partly: transfer from simulation, video and computer-control tasks can broaden the distribution, but data such as touch and force, which video and demonstrations cannot supply, is a real hard constraint.
cruxes.would_change_if: A team shows that a policy trained on vision plus simulation alone reaches human level, without extra tactile data, on real tasks that need fine force control.

cruxes.question: Does academia still have genuinely differentiated room in foundation-model research, or is it already locked out by the oligopoly's scale?
cruxes.my_position: General pre-training is basically locked in the hands of 3-4 labs, but narrow-domain, verifiable work with modest compute needs, such as evaluation, interpretability and RL reward design, remains open.
cruxes.would_change_if: An academic team, using far less compute than frontier labs, produces a training or evaluation method widely adopted by industry, as DPO or FlashAttention were.

taste_advice: Do not trust probe results that merely 'look like a signal'; design experiments that can show causal use; this is what SAEs losing to linear probes taught me.

pairwise.why: Evaluation is the precondition for trusting any capability judgment; world models are still at the validation stage.
Embodied AI is the fundamentally uncertain extrapolation that I admit; evaluation is the common foundation of all judgments.
The world model (video prediction) is itself a scalable objective; embodied AI is more of a downstream application.
Video prediction is a general scalable objective; a specific action representation is only an architecture choice.
Simulation is a general lever for broadening the distribution; embodied robots are one application of it.
RL already has verifiable scaling curves; even the measurement methods for RSI are immature.
Understanding is closer to language reasoning and more verifiable; generation products already show signs of commoditization.
Pre-training is the source of capability; evaluation only measures capability and does not create it.
Scaffolding will be absorbed by models; learning mechanisms (credit assignment and so on) are more fundamental.
Safety evaluation directly sets the deployment red lines, and it is a field I personally bet on by writing essays.
I have taken no public position on autonomous driving; for embodied AI I at least have my own framework to use.
